answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed trail-warden season on a real mountain path lined with juniper, where the warden carves a uniquely numbered basalt waymarker and logs repairs in a cedar-bound ledger countersigned by the park authority. Random spot-checks summon the holder to their own trail within a day, and one person cannot maintain two distant trails at once. The trail fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so every extra fake identity costs another real trail, another season of labor, another live human, and twice the prior fee.
